chunks: Humayd ibn al-Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Hamzah ibn Humran from al-Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i from Abdullah ibn Muhraz, the seller of Qalanis, who said:

A man bequeathed to me (as executor) and left five hundred dirhams or six hundred dirhams, and left a daughter, and said to me, 'The paternal relatives (asabah) are in Syria.' So I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that, so he said: 'Give the daughter half, and the other half to the paternal relatives.'

So when I arrived in Kufa, I informed our companions of his saying, so they said, 'He was dissimulating (taqaya) for you.' So I gave the other half to the daughter. Then I went for Hajj and met Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and I informed him with what our companions had said, and I informed him that I had handed over the other half to the daughter. So he said: 'You did well. I only gave you the ruling out of fear of the paternal relatives being upon you.'

key_terms.أَحْسَنْتَ: You did well / You were correct
key_terms.اتَّقَاكَ: He dissimulated (taqiyah) for you / He was cautious on your behalf
key_terms.عَصَبَة: Paternal agnatic relatives who inherit when there are no direct descendants

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of taqiyah in the context of inheritance rulings in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the distinction between the Imam's actual legal ruling (fatwa) and his precautionary ruling (ra'y) in inheritance distribution. While the daughter is entitled to half and the asabah (paternal male relatives) to the other half in the absence of other heirs, the Imam advised giving the full share to the daughter to avoid potential disputes with the stronger asabah, a practice known as 'taqiyah' in legal application. This demonstrates the pragmatic flexibility in Shia jurisprudence where context influences the practical execution of divine law.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin iyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Abdullah Bin Bukeyr, from Hama Bin Humran, from Abdul Hameed Al Taiy, from Abdullah Bin Muhra Bayaa Al Qalanis who said,

‘A man bequeathed to me (to be an executor) and left five hundred Dirhams, or six hundred Dirhams, and left a daughter, and said to me, ‘Paternal relatives are at Syria’. So I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about that, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Give the daughter half, and give the other half to the paternal relatives’.

So when I proceeded to Al-Kufa, I informed our companions of his<sup>asws</sup> speech, so they said, ‘(Out of) dissimulation for you’. So I gave the other half to the daughter, then I went for Hajj. So I met Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and informed him<sup>asws</sup> with what our companions had said, and I informed him<sup>asws</sup> that I had handed over the other half to the daughter’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You have done good. But rather I<sup>asws</sup> was dissimulative to you out of fear of the paternal relatives over you’.
en.sarwar: 7. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from ‘Abd Alfah ibn Jabalah from ‘Abd Alfah ibn Bukayr from Hamzah ibn Humran from ‘Abd ai-Hamid af-Ta”iy from ‘Abd Affah ibn Muhriz Bayya‘ ai-Qaianisiy who has narrated the foiiowing:

“A man made a will about five hundred dirhams or six hundred dirhams, leaving behind his daughter, and told me that his paternal relatives are in Sham. I asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about it and he (the Imam) said, ‘Give one-half to his daughter and the other half to his paternal relatives.’

When I returned to al-Kufah, I told our people about it and they said that he (the Imam) has said so because of taqiyah (fear). I then gave the other half to his daughter; then I went for al-Hajj and visited abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. I informed him (the Imam) about what our people had said and that I have given the other half also to his daughter. He (the Imam) said, ‘You have done good. I gave the fatwa that I did because of fear for you from the paternal relatives.’”
